subject: API model retirement — ops plan & comms checklist
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: API model retirement — ops plan & comms checklist

Team —

We need to lock down the ops and comms plan for the planned retirement of the text-gen-v1 family (public API alias: tgen-v1). Goal: retire the family with a predictable, low-friction migration path for customers and minimal spike in support/latency. Draft timeline below, attached is a granular checklist (2026-12-05_model-retirement-checklist.xlsx) and a customer comms draft. Please review and comment with explicit accepts/blockers by EOD Monday.

High-level timeline (proposed)
- 2027-01-10: Announce 90-day retirement notice to affected customers (public blog + direct to HubSpot lists)
- 2027-01-17: SDK bump and migration guide published (python/js/Rust)
- 2027-02-15: Begin automated routing to fallback model variants for unsupported requests
- 2027-04-10: Final shutdown of tgen-v1 pool (requests return 410 + migration hint)

Critical asks by function
- Engineering (karthik): finalize compatibility matrix and ensure server-side 410 payload includes SDK-friendly guidance (code snippets + migration headers). Confirm batching/kv-cache impacts for common seq-lens.
- Product (laura/soojin): approve customer-facing blog + internal FAQ; define exception gating (see below).
- CS/Sales (marissa/stephanie): prepare outreach cadence and targeted 1:1 for top 30 customers (we'll seed with HubSpot list).
- Docs/DevX (hannah): publish migration guide and a short how-to video; mark breaking changes clearly.

Exception gating proposal (TL;DR: narrow, temporary)
- Exceptions allowed only for customers with active enterprise contracts and demonstrated technical blocker (e.g., model mismatch causing regression >10% on eval suite).
- Exceptions expire with final shutdown date; require signed addendum and FRA (feature rollback agreement).

Telemetry & rollback criteria
- Trigger: >3x support tickets on auth/400/500 for a given customer cohort in a 48h window OR 25%+ regression in prompt-based automatic evals across random sample.
- Rollback path: re-enable tgen-v1 in a limited pool for affected customers for up to 7 days while we remediate.

Open questions (please answer inline)
1) Is the 90-day public notice sufficient for regulated customers? (legal/contracts concerns)
2) Can we publish an SDK minor release that auto-translates obvious input flags (e.g., max_tokens -> max_new_tokens) to reduce friction?
3) Do we need a soft-deprecation mode (warning header but still serve) for the first 30 days?

Attachments: 2026-12-05_model-retirement-checklist.xlsx, customer-comm-draft_v2.md

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Product (Inference)
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: API model retirement — ops plan & comms checklist

On Fri, 05 Dec 2026 at 09:12, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> We need to lock down the ops and comms plan for the planned retirement of the text-gen-v1 family (public API alias: tgen-v1).

Thanks — high level looks good. A few technical clarifications and blockers: 

- Compatibility matrix: we have three breaking vectors: tokenizer changes, default sampling / temperature semantics, and kv-cache layout for resumed sessions. We'll publish a matrix but the kv-cache issue is the big one — it means session resumption isn't binary-compatible across v1 -> v2 for customers using long-lived sessions. That's the main ask from CS to signal to customers.
- Soft-deprecation vs 90-day notice: we *can* publish warning headers for the first 30 days (adds ~1% latency and small header surface). Acceptable tradeoff if Product wants the smoother UX.
- SDK auto-compat shim: feasible for python/js for obvious renames; Rust will be a patch release but we should document fallback. Engineering estimate: 2 sprints for stable shim + tests (target: 2027-01-17).
- Rollback pool: we need a runway to keep a tiny pool (2x minimum healthy) for emergency exceptions. That has OPEX impact; estimate $8k/month. Approve budget?

I'll update the checklist with these technical rows and add CI jobs to run interop tests across the top 30 customers' test prompts.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: API model retirement — ops plan & comms checklist

On Fri, Dec 5, 2026 at 11:03 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — high level looks good. A few technical clarifications and blockers: 

Quick customer-side notes:
- Top 30 list attached in HubSpot (HubSpot: CONTACT-5329). We should schedule 2-weekly outreach: notify -> one week -> book migration call. Stephanie and I will split outreach: I take platform customers; Stephanie takes app/platform partners.
- Enterprise customers: expect requests for exceptions for data residency and inference determinism. We should require a migration runbook + perf/regression baseline before granting exception — the gating language in the checklist is fine.
- Suggested comm language: be explicit that SDK patch will try to auto-translate 'obvious' flags but customers should run their regression test. We'll add a short snippet to the comms draft showing the SDK shim.
- Customer-facing migration webinar: recommend Jan 20 (two days after SDK publish) at 0900 PT; we can record.

Questions/asks for legal/sales ops (cc internal):
- Need a short template addendum for exceptions (we can use existing emergency-access template).
- Can we pre-authorize a credit bucket for top 5 customers if they hit unexpected perf regressions? (Laura to decide.)

I'll draft the outreach email and share the calendar invites by Monday.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: API model retirement — ops plan & comms checklist

Thanks all — great discussion. Final decisions and owners below: 

Decisions
- Approve 90-day public notice with a 30-day soft-deprecation (warning header only) during the first 30 days. Product will publish the blog + FAQ on 2027-01-10. (Owner: Soojin)
- Engineering to implement SDK auto-compat shim for python/js. Ship as minor SDK bump on 2027-01-17. (Owner: Karthik + DevX)
- Exceptions: allowed only with signed addendum and technical runbook; exceptions are temporary and expire on 2027-04-10. Legal will draft addendum. (Owner: Marissa + Legal)
- Emergency rollback pool authorized; finance approves up to $10k/month for retention during the retirement window. (Owner: Karthik to budget)

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Soojin: finalize blog + comms + publish checklist to internal docs (due 2026-12-10)
- Karthik: add interop CI and CI jobs for top30 prompts, + rollout for warning headers (due 2026-12-22)
- Marissa: outreach cadence and calendar for top30; draft exception addendum template with Sales Ops (due 2026-12-15)
- Hannah: migration guide and 3-min how-to video (due 2027-01-17)
- Stephanie: schedule migration webinar for 2027-01-20 and coordinate recording (due 2026-12-17)

I'll coordinate with Finance and Legal on the exception addendum and credit bucket. If there are no blockers by EOD Monday, we'll lock the timeline and send the public notice draft to comms for review.

Laura
VP, Product Management
Redwood Inference
